newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX eases, ends string of record highs.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX eases, ends string of record highs.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday gave up one percent of the eight percent it gained in the last six record breaking sessions as the expected correction reached the market, traders and analysts said.
The BUX index which briefly jumped to a new trading high of 7,303.26 points, finished at a preliminary 7,219.20 points, down 77.44 points or 1.06 percent.

"The anticipated correction reached the market, but the Dow's fall (on Wednesday) and the dollar's weakening during the session have contributed," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett (Budapest) Rt.
The dollar fell below 189 forints from its opening at 189.58/63 to the forint.
She said that turnover was boosted by agency crosses but interest towards the market has weakened.
"There would have been more buyers but at lower prices only," Keresztesi said.
Gaspar Czako, analyst at Eastbrokers in Budapest said the spot market's fall was of a technical nature and did not come as a surprise.
"This is a technical correction... which could be expected as the market ran away a little bit," Czako said.
The analyst said he saw no reason for the market's long-term upper trend to break but some more correction might come with a support level seen between 6,800 and 6,900 points.
Pharmaceuticals stocks were among heavy losers, with Richter giving up 475 forints to finish at 17,150.

Egis fell 305 forints to close at 13,995 after a daily newspaper report that with its majority owner it bought a Polish drugs factory. Human, one of the market's top gainers recently eased 85 forints to end at 3,775.
Elsewhere on the market, hotel chain Danubius, tile manufacturer Zalakeramia, machinery firm Mezogep and plastics group Pannonplast bucked the falling trend and closed a shade firmer.
Danubius closed at 5,800 forints, up 50; Mezogep at 3,350 forints, up 30; Zalakeramia at 7,510, up 60 and Pannonplast at 9,550, up 75.
On the futures market, BUX index contracts tumbled for all maturities. September BUX fell 190.5 points to close at 7,350 points, while December BUX gave up 209.5 points to end at 7,780.
